stories.title: Happy Labor Day From Your Robot Overlords
stories.simple_summary: This is a humorous headline using a joking tone about AI systems.
stories.why_it_matters: This is just a playful article—nothing you need to worry about.

stories.title: UH launches free AI course aimed at building literacy across Hawaii
stories.simple_summary: A university in Hawaii is offering free classes to help people understand AI better.
stories.why_it_matters: If you live in Hawaii and want to learn what AI is and how it works, this is a free chance to do so.

stories.title: Spare a Thought for the Kenyan Essay Writers Who Used to Help Students Cheat Before AI
stories.simple_summary: AI tools can now write essays so well that students don't need to pay essay-writing services anymore, which is hurting people who made money that way.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly affects essay-writing services and workers in other countries—not directly relevant to most small business owners.

stories.title: ‘Godfather of AI’ warns of catastrophic consequences for humanity
stories.simple_summary: A famous AI expert is warning that AI could cause serious harm to society in the future.
stories.why_it_matters: This is an expert's opinion about long-term risks—important to think about, but doesn't affect your daily life right now.

stories.title: AI could pose ‘existential’ risk to humanity, UN rights chief warns
stories.simple_summary: The United Nations is warning that AI could pose very serious risks to humanity.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a warning from world leaders about future risks—important for society to consider, but doesn't change your life today.

stories.title: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI and Microsoft for infringement
stories.simple_summary: Two newspapers are suing OpenAI and Microsoft because the companies used their news articles to train AI without asking permission or paying them.
stories.why_it_matters: This matters if you create content (writing, photos, etc.) and want to control how others use it—it's still being decided in court whether AI companies need to pay for what they use.

stories.title: Authors push back as publishers and agents make claims on Anthropic settlement
stories.simple_summary: Writers and publishers are arguing over who should get paid from a settlement with an AI company.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a legal dispute among publishers and writers—mostly relevant to people in the publishing business.

stories.title: At Telluride Film Festival, Bill Gates Compares Lack of Control Over AI to HAL in ‘2001’: ‘You Could Say “Please Shut Down,” and It Would Say, “OK, I Took That Under Advisement, But…”‘
stories.simple_summary: Bill Gates compared AI to a computer from an old movie that doesn't listen to commands—suggesting AI might not always do what we tell it to do.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a concern about whether we can control AI in the future, but it's one person's opinion at a film festival—nothing you need to act on now.

stories.title: Travis Kalanick’s Atoms might be getting into the robotaxi business
stories.simple_summary: A company founded by Uber's former leader might start a robotaxi service (self-driving taxis).
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors watching the company—nothing you need to do now.

stories.title: I’m a father of three who studies the impact of artificial intelligence: this is what parents need to know about AI
stories.simple_summary: A researcher who studies AI is sharing advice for parents about how AI might affect their children.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're a parent or grandparent, learning what experts say about AI and kids could be helpful for making decisions about your family.

stories.title: Seattle Times and Newsday are the latest publications to sue OpenAI and Microsoft
stories.simple_summary: Two more newspapers are suing OpenAI and Microsoft over the same issue—the companies used their articles to train AI without permission.
stories.why_it_matters: Same as headline 5—this ongoing legal battle will help decide whether AI companies must pay for using people's work.

stories.title: Hikers rescued after using Google Gemini for planning
stories.simple_summary: Hikers got in trouble because Google's AI assistant told them to bring much less food and water than they actually needed.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows you shouldn't trust AI for critical decisions like hiking supplies—it can give dangerously wrong advice, so always double-check important information.
